description: Product token bindings to the existing canonical design-system CSS. Literal values are product-specific additions or reviewed compatibility overrides. Rule order preserves the existing token cascade.

Tell the user agent the app paints on a dark surface by default. Without
     this hint the browser fills the empty document with its own white "blank"
     state between document swap and CSS variable resolution during F5 reloads,
     producing a visible white flash before the shader/background paints (#302).

Mode-aware shadow ink (#1295 Category C1). Dark = pure black (the historical
     hardcoded shadow ink), so rgb(var(--shadow-ink-rgb) / α) is byte-identical to the
     prior rgba(0, 0, 0, α) in dark/+HC/forced-colors. The light block re-points it to
     the DS warm shadow ink (20 30 25) so component drop-shadows adapt in Light.

============================================================
   DESIGN-SYSTEM TOKEN TIERS 2–4 (#1292) — scales · semantic · component
   ------------------------------------------------------------
   SOURCE OF TRUTH: this file (globals.css) is the single emitted stylesheet
   the product ships (imported once at app/layout.tsx). The standalone
   design-system/keiko-*.css files are the human-readable REFERENCE mirror,
   not a build input — nothing imports them. This block consolidates the
   middle + top of the four-tier token architecture into the product so the
   reference and the runtime stop diverging (epic #1290, blueprint #1291,
   docs/design-system/token-component-reuse-map.md §1).

   Strategy = EXTEND, never fork: every alias below resolves to a Tier-1
   primitive already defined in the :root above, so the rendered product is
   byte-identical until components are migrated to consume these names (the
   migrations are scoped to #1293–#1298). Because the primitives already
   redefine themselves for the light theme, prefers-contrast / in-app
   high-contrast, and forced-colors, these aliases inherit all modes
   automatically — there is no per-mode duplication to keep in sync. The
   globals.css.test.ts suite pins this set
   against design-system/keiko-semantic-tokens.css as a drift gate; adding a
   second :root token source (a parallel namespace) is forbidden by the epic
   reuse gate. ============================================================
── SCALE · SPACING — 2-based rhythm, mode-independent ──
── SCALE · RADIUS (alias — primitives own the values) ──
── SCALE · TYPE WEIGHT ──
── SCALE · LINE-HEIGHT ──
── SCALE · TYPE SIZE — role-named ramp, 11px floor ──
── SCALE · OPACITY ──
── SCALE · BLUR ──
── SCALE · MOTION (reduced-motion handled globally below) ──
── SCALE · Z-INDEX — named layers, closes the raw-z-index gap ──
── SCALE · BREAKPOINTS — canonical media-query reference values ──
── SCALE · DENSITY — comfortable default, compact overridden below ──

── SEMANTIC — the layer product code should consume. All resolve to
        mode-aware primitives, so correct in dark · light · +HC · forced-colors ──
── COMPONENT — one resolved name per component decision ──

WCAG 2.2 AA (RB-14) — the window zoom cluster (.win-zoom) rests at opacity:0.72,
     which composites this badge's text toward the window surface. --text-tertiary then
     measured only 3.45:1 in a real browser (jsdom axe cannot see it). A primary+secondary
     mix clears 4.5:1 at that resting opacity in dark (6.15:1) and light (4.97:1) while
     staying dimmer than the window title; it resolves per-theme through the referenced
     tokens (dark/light/HC), and brightens to --text-primary on hover.

Issue #1297 — Design System 0.4.0 data-visualisation palette (design-system/keiko-dataviz.css).
     Categorical hues at a matched chroma so no single series shouts (order = legend order), a
     single-hue green sequential ramp for magnitude, plus grid/axis tokens. Dark values live here;
     the light-theme block overrides --viz-2..6 and --viz-seq-1..5 for light backgrounds.

Single-source HC palettes — the OS media query and explicit in-app attribute
   below both promote these same primitives, matching the design-system mirror.

============================================================
   Editor theme tokens (#1212) — consumed by the Keiko Editor Monaco runtime (#1193).
   Lifted from design/keiko-editor-tokens.css; EXTENDS the base palette (does not fork it):
   editor chrome reuses --bg/--fg/--danger/--warn/--info, and only the syntax palette plus the
   editor-specific chrome/diff/ghost-text are net-new. Surfaced here so the --ed-* / --ed-syn-*
   custom properties resolve at runtime when the editor mounts (host integration, #1194); the
   Monaco theme reads them via getComputedStyle and embeds no colour literals. Dark is the default;
   the light and high-contrast variants follow the source. High contrast is exposed both through
   prefers-contrast and [data-hc="more"], matching the design-system source.
   ============================================================

#1295 C1 — DS warm shadow ink for Light (same 20 30 25 the light --shadow-card/-pop
     already use), so component drop-shadows routed through rgb(var(--shadow-ink-rgb) / α)

#1295 C3 — Light dialog scrim. Centralises the shared light backdrop value the
     per-component overrides used (.dlg-overlay/.wf-dialog-overlay/.mc-dialog-backdrop),
     so the base scrim rules routed to var(--overlay-scrim) adapt in Light.
